crime_highlights: Mr. Julian had punched her with a closed fist on her ear, breaking her glasses
the punch knocked Ms. Michael off the chair where she was seated
Mr. Julian kept hitting her with both fists and kicking her on her knees and legs
The attack terrified Ms. Michael and she fled to a neighbour's house, bleeding
she has suffered lasting psychological effects
rationale_highlights: Mr. Julian's history is, as the Defence pointed out to me, a tragically common profile of abuse, dislocation, chaos and discrimination
The harms done to him in his childhood and youth were not his fault
I am required to approach Mr. Julian's sentencing differently
I recognize that like so many First Nations people, you have had a difficult and challenging life
given all the factors that I have taken into account, including the Gladue factors, that it is a fit and appropriate sentence in this case
note: Gladue factors weighed but custody imposed

crime_highlights: Ms. Brooks went after her, tackling her to the ground and again punching and kicking her
was attacked by Ms. Brooks and knocked to the ground
Ms. Syliboy was badly injured in the attack and spent one night in the hospital
She received several stitches for a laceration to the area above her eyebrow
Ms. Syliboy sustained two fractured ribs and chipped teeth
rationale_highlights: In this case there is a reasonable alternative to sending Ms. Brooks to jail
Jail will separate her from her child and make parental absence and family dislocation the experience of yet another generation
members of her family underwent the Indian Residential School experience
As a sentencing judge, I have the power and obligation to influence the treatment of this Aboriginal offender
note: Conditional sentence imposed; Gladue effect stated in para 76

crime_highlights: He, with two other males, one a youth, the other an adult, attacked and robbed L.S. of percocet medication
L.S. received some cuts, scrapes and bruises from being punched and kicked during the attack
L.S. was lured out to a meeting that he thought would be with H.N.
rationale_highlights: a community-based sentence with conditions is most appropriate for J.J.P., especially given his circumstances as an aboriginal youth
note: Very brief Gladue treatment; only para 5 addresses it
